about: Insights from 'A Multi-Stakeholder Approach for Urban Heat Resilience: Singapore's Experience' (Global Heat Health Information Network Southeast Asia Hub, June 2026), each traced to the primary source behind it. stage.js turns this into data/inbox/2026-11-singapore-brief/sources.json; verify-sources.yml checks every term on its page; apply.js uses a claim only when every term it rests on was found. No individual is named; governments are not ranked.

claims.text: The national heat stress advisory was developed by the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment and the National Environment Agency with the Ministry of Health and its expert panel on heat stress.

claims.where: Worked example: Singapore (result); lever heatrules example
claims.text: In September 2024 the rules were revised to follow the advisory's three levels: at 33 °C or above, at least 15 minutes' rest an hour is recommended for heavy work; new workers acclimatise over at least 7 days; and construction sites with contracts of S$5 million or more, shipyards and process plants keep their own WBGT meters.

In March 2026 a Heat Resilience Policy Office was set up to coordinate action across agencies, oversee research and draft a heat resilience action plan across infrastructure, health, economic and social sectors.

alt: air-conditioned cooling spaces in community centres
claims.text: Since March 2025 a heatwave is declared when the daily maximum reaches at least 35 °C and the daily mean at least 29 °C for three days in a row; air-conditioned cooling spaces then open in community centres.
A taskforce of 37 public agencies prepares and carries out the response.

claims.where: Funders: Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment record
claims.text: Its S$40 million 'Adapting to Heat Impacts' funding initiative (2026) supports research on heat impacts and community heat resilience.

claims.where: Funders: Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment record
claims.text: The S$40 million initiative sits within the RIE2030 Heat Resilience R&D Programme, which has one pillar on infrastructure and one on heat's impact on society.

claims.where: Practical actions / worked example: employers beyond the rules
claims.text: Changi Airport Group describes cooling rest areas, hydration stations, protective wear, training and extra rest on hot days for about 30,000 airside workers.
Singapore's military has managed heat injuries in training for decades; a 2023 review traces how those policies developed.

claims.where: Learning agenda: work under way on the true count of heat illness
claims.text: Singapore's HEAT-MAP study is building a fuller picture of how common heat-related illness is now and could become, with findings used to help older people recognise its symptoms.

claims.where: Learning agenda: work under way on lived experience of heat at home
claims.text: A household study in Singapore looks at how residents, including those in rental flats, experience urban heat.

claims.where: Organisations: new record for the Southeast Asia hub
claims.text: The Global Heat Health Information Network's hub for Southeast Asia, based in Singapore, shares heat-health evidence and practice across the region; Philanthropy Asia Alliance supports its work in countries including Indonesia and Thailand.

claims.where: Who is at risk / practical: delivery riders
rests_on: Few firms make similar concessions in hot weather
not even allowed to go into restaurants
claims.text: Few delivery platforms in Asia make concessions to riders in hot weather, and riders may not be allowed into restaurants to pick up orders, get a drink of water or use the washroom, according to a source quoted by Eco-Business.

claims.where: Who is at risk: delivery riders
claims.text: Some platforms say they do not penalise riders who turn down orders in challenging weather.
